text: The Nederlandse Spoorwegen (NS) Class 1300 was a Dutch locomotive in service for 48 years, from 1952 until 2000. It was built simultaneously with the NS Class 1100 at Alsthom and based on the SNCF Class CC 7100. The Class 1300 is a larger 6-axle, Co′Co′, version of the Class 1100. The first locomotive, 1301, was delivered in 1952 and was first used at the opening of the electric service between Zwolle and Groningen. After less than a year in service, 1303 was damaged beyond repair when it collided with EMU 642 at Weesp on June 19, 1953. Following this accident, Alsthom delivered a new locomotive that was originally intended for the SNCF as a CC 7100; 1303 was scrapped on the spot, though some of its equipment was salvaged for use in the replacement locomotive 1311. The locomotives numbered 1312 to 1316 were delivered in 1956 in a Berlin blue colour scheme, while the 1952 deliveries were initially painted turquoise but were repainted Berlin blue in 1955. During the 1980s, the entire Class 1300 underwent prolonging maintenance and were painted yellow with a large NS logo on the side. All locomotives in the class were named after a Dutch city. In 2000, the last locomotives were withdrawn from service. The locomotives 1302, 1304, 1312, and 1315 have been preserved. In 2015, number 1304 returned to service for private operator HSL Logistik, but broke down in February 2016 due to operator error. In late 2018, it was repaired by replacing a few traction motors and has since been deployed by the Fairtrains foundation for occasional transfers. Fairtrains' objective is to restore and preserve museum equipment using revenues from its operations. Number 1315 is the next to be refurbished and is expected to be operational again in 2019. Number 1312 serves as the working representative of the class at the Dutch Railway Museum, with number 1302 acting as a spare part donor.
